purpose: Workload-level warm timing of the CHS likelihood-and-gradient on the estimation fixture (tests/test_missing_observed_factors.py _model(2, law, MOMENTS), nonlinear=0.05), translog versus stable_translog, identical data and parameters. Supplements the reviewer's kernel microbenchmark (native-resource-comparison.json), whose per-call cost is dominated by dispatch at the 10 microsecond scale.
command: for law in translog stable_translog translog stable_translog; do zsh -ic "cap pixi run -e tests-cpu python <scratchpad>/time_loglike.py $law 200"; done  (one fresh process per run; first call includes compilation; warm = mean of 200 subsequent synchronized calls)
assessment: Warm likelihood-and-gradient time per call: translog 2.75 / 2.63 ms, stable_translog 1.85 / 2.51 ms; the run-to-run spread of the same law (0.1 to 0.9 ms) exceeds the difference between laws. Peak RSS differs by about 1 percent. No workload-level runtime or memory regression is detectable at the 10 percent trigger.
